p.i: Verf. 15. Væ potanti socium suum, ó addens ardorem tuum, atque etiam inebriando, ad intuendum nudata illorum.

main_text.p: § 1. Digito quasi monstrat Index quosdam, malè habentes quemcunque socium, aut proximum; quibus monet judicium paratum. Potator socii aut proximi sui audit, qui ut divino supplicio dignus hic primò loco notatur. Hebr. משקה רעהו. Peccatum notatur, ut pro objecto studii sui habens, socium, vel proximum, aut si ita mavis, quemcunque alterum: omnia hæc enim notat vox [illegible, ~2 letters]; vertitur enim socius, Jud. 14:20. proximus, Lev. 29:18. & alter Exod. 21:18. Homo homini debet communicationem veritatis: quod si quis alium seducere laboret, peccat contra legem secundæ tabulæ. page.notes: The Hebrew phrase in § 1 (משקה רעהו) is copied from the scan. The Hebrew word after "vox" is too faint to read reliably and is marked illegible. The printed "socium,· aut" has a stray mark after the comma, which is treated as a comma. The long s is read as s throughout (e.g. "sit", "monstrat", "supplicio"), so "fit" is taken as "sit" from context. The "2." and "B." lines are an outline, copied as list lines. No marginal notes, no woodcut, no stamps.
